text: Midcourse test track one Hi everyone My presentation today is about two alternative and quite strange food festivals that take place around the world But not in the way you might think I'm interested in these types of festivals because they are a strange way to celebrate food and are very popular Have you ever heard of the night of the radishes? It's a festival that takes place in my hometown Oaxaca in southern Mexico and it is over a century old for the festival we decorate radishes a vegetable that's red on the outside and white on the inside But we don't eat them The festival takes place on the 23rd of December and seems to get more and more popular every year So how did it begin? Well people working in markets wanted to attract shoppers to the town square So they cut radishes into the shape of people or animals They were very popular and in 1897 they decided to make it a festival and that tradition lives on to this day The radishes are larger than normal and they are picked around the 18th of December Artists only have a few days to get their radishes ready and the person who has the best radish wins a 12,000 peso prize The most amazing thing about this event is how popular it is People wait hours just to see the radishes The second festival I want to talk about is called La Tomatina This takes place in Spain in this small town of Búñol about 9,000 people live in the town but during La Tomatina thousands of tourists visit the region just to be part of the occasion So what is it? Well, it's a huge food fight with tomatoes people believe La Tomatina started around 1945 when a large public food fight took place A celebration was taking place in the village with people dressed in giant heads Some young people made the big head of someone fall off and he got very angry He tried to run after the young people but fell into a market stall selling tomatoes So the man started throwing tomatoes at the young people Then more people started to join in and he turned into a huge tomato fight The people of Búñol enjoyed it so much that they did it again the next year It became a big festival in 1952 What does the festival consist of? On the day big lorries filled with tomatoes arrive in the main square of the town How much tomato do you think they use for the fight? 120 thousand kilos The fight starts at 11 a.m. and it ends when someone fires a large gun called a cannon These are just two of the many strange food festivals around the world They are strange because people don't eat the food at these festivals They use it to make things or throw it at each other But these festivals are enormous fun for all generations and are a great alternative for people looking for something different
